experiment: Cryo-EM single-particle reconstruction of apo Mt UvrD1 dimer (2D/3D classification; compact and extended classes)
buffer: phosphate buffer, 5% glycerol, 75 mM NaCl (dialysis after BS3 crosslinking)
construct_or_mutation: Mycobacterium tuberculosis UvrD1, wild type, oxidized (C451-C451 disulfide dimer); BS3-crosslinked
other_conditions: 6 µM UvrD1 (monomer units); compact 4.0 Å masked/5.0 Å unmasked, extended 4.8 Å masked/7.2 Å unmasked; related structures: 2IS6 (open Ec UvrD comparison); compact map EMD-46752, extended map EMD-46753 (no PDB for extended)
dynamics_type: 2B-2B-linked dimer flexibility; compact vs extended subunit arrangement
alt_state_structure: 9DCI: apo compact dimer conformation (Data availability); extended conformation deposited as map only (EMD-46753), no PDB id
author_claim: Apo UvrD1 dimers exist in symmetric compact and extended forms, and the lower, asymmetric resolution of the extended form indicates substantial flexibility across the 2B-2B interface.
anchor: The apo UvrD1 dimer is observed in symmetric compact and extended forms indicating substantial flexibility.
locator: Abstract; Results 'Apo UvrD1 Dimers Exist in At Least Two Conformations'; conditions: Materials and Methods, Cryo-Electron Microscopy
caveat_note: Mt UvrD1 is a homolog (42% identity to Ec UvrD) and the entry is a short E. coli UvrD fragment, so the result is not target evidence. Static cryo-EM classes show conformational heterogeneity but not exchange timescale. Residue numbers (e.g., C451) cannot be mapped to the entry sequence. pH not given for the cryo-EM buffer.

experiment: Cryo-EM reconstruction of DNA-bound Mt UvrD1 dimer (leading vs trailing subunit 2B conformations)
buffer: phosphate buffer, 5% glycerol, 75 mM NaCl (dialysis after BS3 crosslinking)
construct_or_mutation: Mycobacterium tuberculosis UvrD1, wild type, oxidized dimer; BS3-crosslinked
other_conditions: 6 µM UvrD1 (monomer units); 5.9 Å masked/7.7 Å unmasked, higher-resolution dsDNA-masked map 4.9 Å masked/6.5 Å unmasked; 2B rotation apo compact (open) vs trailing (closed) ~154°; leading vs trailing 147° with distinct axis; related structures: 2IS6; maps EMD-46797, EMD-46799
dynamics_type: 2B subdomain rotation / symmetry-broken conformations upon DNA binding
alt_state_structure: 9DES: DNA-bound dimer with leading subunit (new 2B conformation) and trailing subunit (closed 2B) (Data availability; Fig. 3E)
author_claim: DNA binding breaks the C2 symmetry of the dimer, with leading and trailing subunits adopting distinct 2B conformations related by a ~147° rotation about a different axis.
anchor: The leading and trailing subunit 2B domains are related by a 147° rotation, but with a distinct axis of rotation
locator: Results 'The Structure of DNA-Bound UvrD1 Dimer'; Fig. 3E; conditions: Materials and Methods, Cryo-Electron Microscopy
caveat_note: Homolog (Mt UvrD1), not the E. coli entry fragment; conformational states are static cryo-EM snapshots at moderate resolution, with no rates or populations. DNA duplex density has lower local resolution, suggesting multiple orientations. Temperature and pH not stated for this sample.

experiment: Cryo-EM reconstruction of DNA-bound constitutively monomeric Mt UvrD1 C451A (closed 2B, compared with dimer)
buffer: phosphate buffer, 5% glycerol, 75 mM NaCl (dialysis after BS3 crosslinking)
construct_or_mutation: Mycobacterium tuberculosis UvrD1 C451A (monomeric mutant); BS3-crosslinked
other_conditions: 5.6 Å masked/7.0 Å unmasked; model built from AlphaFold prediction aligned to closed Ec UvrD–DNA; imaged on Krios; related structures: 2IS6; map EMD-46850
dynamics_type: 2B subdomain large rotation between monomer–DNA (closed, DNA-contacting) and dimer lead subunit; autoinhibition
alt_state_structure: 9DGY: inhibited DNA-bound monomer with closed 2B contacting duplex DNA (Data availability; Fig. 4A)
author_claim: The monomer–DNA complex has the 2B domain positioned to contact duplex DNA, which is mutually exclusive with dimerization and likely autoinhibitory, so the 2B domain swivels out upon dimerization.
anchor: Hence, the 2B–DNA interaction and UvrD1 dimerization are competitive and mutually exclusive processes.
locator: Results 'Structure of the Inhibited Mt UvrD1 Monomer Bound to a DNA Junction'; Fig. 4; conditions: Materials and Methods
caveat_note: Homolog; density is fitted with an AlphaFold-based model aligned to the Ec UvrD closed structure at modest resolution, so the 2B placement is partly model-driven. The 2B rotation is inferred by comparing separate structures, not by observing exchange. C451A is a mutant that prevents dimerization.

experiment: Analytical sedimentation velocity (c(s)) of Ec UvrD(R421C) +/- DTT at 175 nM
ligand_or_partner: apo (no DNA) for sedimentation; helicase assays with 3′-(dT) 20 -18 bp DNA
construct_or_mutation: Escherichia coli UvrD R421C in Cys-less UvrD background
other_conditions: 42,000 rpm, An50Ti rotor, Proteome Lab XL-A; 175 nM total protein; stopped-flow helicase assays: 12.5 nM monomer units with 25 nM DNA (and reverse), helicase active only when dimerized; related structures: 2IS6
population: ~41% dimer in absence of DTT; monomer only with DTT (175 nM total protein)
author_claim: Ec UvrD(R421C) forms a disulfide-linked dimer and becomes an active helicase under oxidizing conditions, supporting a conserved 2B–2B dimer interface.
anchor: but in the absence of DTT, ~41% of the protein forms dimers
locator: Results 'The 2B–2B Dimer Interface Is Conserved in Ec UvrD'; Fig. 5B top; conditions: Materials and Methods, Analytical Sedimentation
caveat_note: Full-length engineered Cys mutant of Ec UvrD, not the isolated 49-residue entry fragment; residue positions R421/V425 cannot be mapped onto the entry sequence, so residues_entry is empty. The measurement reports oligomeric state (association equilibrium), not conformational exchange kinetics. pH of the sedimentation buffer is not given in the main text (Buffer T defined in SI).

experiment: Analytical sedimentation velocity (c(s)) of Ec UvrD(V425C) +/- DTT at 155 nM (control)
construct_or_mutation: Escherichia coli UvrD V425C in Cys-less UvrD background
other_conditions: 42,000 rpm; 155 nM protein; cysteine placed by sequence alignment with UvrD1; no oxidative helicase activation (Fig. 5D)
author_claim: V425C does not show redox-dependent dimerization or oxidative helicase activation, unlike R421C, consistent with a specific conserved 2B–2B interface.
anchor: a different cysteine mutation (V425C) that was made based only on a sequence alignment with UvrD1 does not display redox-dependent dimerization
locator: Results 'The 2B–2B Dimer Interface Is Conserved in Ec UvrD'; Fig. 5B bottom and 5D
caveat_note: Negative result means this particular cysteine position does not crosslink, not that dimerization is absent; geometry of the engineered site may simply not permit a disulfide. Full-length construct; residue not mappable to the entry fragment.
